title: 90-day reliability play experiments backlog — implementation journal
content:
Purpose
This is a running implementation journal for a 90-day reliability "play" program focused on operationalizing SLOs across teams and running short, measurable experiments that change behavior or tooling. Not a polished playbook — working notes, decisions, and next steps.

Background/context
- Business context: product teams expect consistent latency/cost across hosted and dedicated. We need measurable SLOs that map to engineering changes and ops runbooks.
- Problem statement: SLOs exist in theory but inconsistent signal definitions, alerting thresholds, and ownership mean we miss customer-impacting regressions.
- Goal for 90 days: run 6 experiments (2 infra, 2 serving runtime, 2 product/observability) that each have a clear hypothesis, automated measurement, and rollback criteria.

Top-level success metrics (how we’ll know this program worked)
- Two service-level SLOs adopted by three cross-functional teams as primary indicators (latency P95 and error rate)
- Median alert noise reduced by 30% for SLO-driven alerts in pilot services
- Error budget policy exercised at least once and used to trigger an automated canary rollback
- One set of signal transformations (trace->slo metrics) deployed to prod with a documented mapping and tests

Stakeholders & roles
- Program lead / coordinator: Priya Anand (SRE) — overall backlog, meeting cadence, comms
- Engineering partners: Marcus Liang (Serving Runtime), Elena Soto (Platform Eng), Noah Patel (API/Hosted), Sofia Ramirez (Observability)
- Product owners: two feature PMs (TBD) — commit to acceptance criteria for their services
- Engineering managers: responsible for allocating 2 sprint-weeks across their teams for experiments
- Incident commander pool: on-call SRE + service oncall during experiments

90-day schedule (high level)
- Week 0 (planning): finalize experiments, define metrics and instrumentation, wire up dashboards
- Weeks 1–4 (alpha sprint): run experiments 1 & 2, daily 20m standup, capture learnings
- Weeks 5–8 (beta sprint): run experiments 3 & 4, incorporate infra changes, expand sample size
- Weeks 9–12 (prod roll/validation): run experiments 5 & 6 and perform cross-team rollout for successful experiments

Experiment backlog (candidate items — each should be turned into a short ticket with hypothesis/owner/metric/rollback)
1) Unified latency definition experiment (observability)
   - Hypothesis: switching to request_end - request_start (server-side) for latency metric reduces variance vs. client-derived metric by >20%
   - Owner: Sofia Ramirez
   - Metric: P95 latency variance on pilot service (metric: pilot.api.latency.server_ms.p95)
   - Success: variance down 20%, dashboards verified, alert thresholds re-evaluated
   - Rollback: restore client-side metric if discrepancy >15% at any time

2) Prefix KV cache effectiveness A/B (serving runtime)
   - Hypothesis: enabling prefix KV cache for repeat prompts reduces average token generation CPU/GPU time by 12%
   - Owner: Marcus Liang
   - Metric: tokens/sec per GPU, tail latency (p99), and cost-per-token estimate for pilot workload
   - Success: measured cost improvement and no >1.5x increase in p99 latency for cold-starts
   - Rollback: disable cache globally and limit to per-tenant after detection of degraded tail latency

3) Error budget automation for planned deploys (platform + SRE)
   - Hypothesis: gating non-critical deploys when error budget <10% reduces post-deploy customer impact by 40%
   - Owner: Elena Soto + Priya Anand
   - Metric: post-deploy error spike frequency for gated vs non-gated deploys
   - Success: one automated gate exercised, documented policy and rollback path created
   - Rollback: manual override only by oncall lead with postmortem

4) Canary SLO for embeddings endpoint (API/product)
   - Hypothesis: a lightweight canary with synthetic queries catches regressive embeddings quality and latency faster than manual sampling
   - Owner: Noah Patel
   - Metric: canary score drift and p95 latency for canary vs baseline
   - Success: canary triggers a false-positive rate <5% and catches at least one injected regression during test windows
   - Rollback: automatic fallback to previous model variant on canary fail

5) Signal harmonization: traces -> SLO metrics pipeline (observability/infra)
   - Hypothesis: standardizing span tags and mapping to SLO labels reduces onboarding time for new services by >50%
   - Owner: Sofia Ramirez + Elena Soto
   - Metric: time-to-instrument for 2 pilot services; number of mapping errors in automated validation
   - Success: pipeline documented, integration tests in CI, two services instrumented
   - Rollback: run fallback exporter to previous metrics format for 24h while fixes applied

6) Batching / autoscale policy experiments for Dedicated (infrastructure)
   - Hypothesis: adjusting autoscale window and batch sizing reduces cost-per-1M-tokens by 8% at no >5% regression in p95 latency
   - Owner: Marcus Liang + Infrastructure lead (TBD)
   - Metric: cost-per-token, p95 latency across load profiles
   - Success: measurable cost savings validated on a reserved pool
   - Rollback: revert autoscale policy and batch-size to baseline config

Minimum experiment artifact checklist (per experiment)
- Short ticket with hypothesis, owner, success & rollback criteria (Jira key)
- Dashboard with automated test-run and alerts for experiment signals
- One canary job / synthetic runner where applicable
- Acceptance test in CI to prevent accidental merge without feature flag
- Postmortem template filled within 72 hours if experiment causes >1 customer-impacting incident

Dependencies & points of coordination
- Observability team must ship tracer tagging conventions by Week 0 (Sofia)
- Platform infra changes require infra-approved feature flags (Elena)
- Product PMs must sign off on acceptance criteria for any customer-facing SLO changes
- Legal/compliance: changes to telemetry retention must be flagged early (privacy review)

Communication plan
- Weekly one-page digest (email + #sre-program Slack) every Friday with experiment statuses and immediate asks
- Bi-weekly 45m sync: program lead + engineering partners + PMs (Agenda: blockers, signals, go/no-go)
- Incident comms: if an experiment hits rollback criteria, immediately page oncall and Slack #reliability-ops and follow the incident template

Risk log (rolling)
- Risk: noisy signals produce wasted work
  - Mitigation: instrument small sample windows first, use synthetic canaries to validate signal fidelity
- Risk: cross-team bandwidth (teams in feature sprints)
  - Mitigation: ask for protected 2 sprint-weeks; split experiments into smaller 1–2 week sub-experiments
- Risk: metrics mismatches between telemetry sources
  - Mitigation: run side-by-side for one week, automated comparison queries, agreed tolerance window

Open questions / notes to self
- Which two production services are best for pilot? Candidate: hosted-api-auth, embeddings-service. Need PM OK.
- Need concise SLA -> SLO mapping doc for legal + sales; draft exists but needs revision (link above).
- Should we create a dedicated program board in the SRE Jira project? (Pros: visibility, cons: noise) — lean toward yes.

Immediate next actions (this week)
- Convert each experiment to a one-pager ticket (owners assigned) — Priya to create stub tickets by Mon 05/11
- Sofia to finalize tracer tag conventions and publish in Confluence by Wed 05/13
- Marcus to spin up KV cache experiment in staging and report initial perf numbers by Fri 05/15
- Elena to propose feature flag schema for error budget gating by Fri 05/15

Appendix: quick templates
- Experiment ticket template: summary | owner | hypothesis | metric | dashboard link | success | rollback | jira-link
- Postmortem template link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Postmortem+Template

Quick notes from standups (scratchpad)
- 2026-05-12: Marcus: cache warm-up seems good but p99 spikes on 1/50 runs; need better isolation test.
- 2026-05-14: Sofia: trace tag PR open, pending schema update from infra.
- 2026-05-18: Noah: synthetic canary runner ready in staging, will start daily runs next week.

-- end of journal entry 2026-05-24 --

(Notes: This document will be iterated often. Treat as working source of truth for the 90-day program; final playbook to be collated after experiments complete.)
